Rclone Migration RunbookDropbox → Google Drive
Technical Runbook350 GB Server-to-Server Copy
Technical Runbook

Migrating Data from Dropbox to Google Drive with Rclone

A production-ready guide to moving 350 GB of data directly from Dropbox to Google Drive. Rclone performs a server-to-server copy, so files never touch your local hard drive.

Volume
350 GB
Method
Server-to-server
Window
< 24 hours

1. Prerequisites

  • Operating systemWindows, macOS, or Linux.
  • Free storageAt least 350 GB available on the destination Google account.
  • API limitGoogle Drive enforces a 750 GB daily upload limit per user. A 350 GB migration completes comfortably within one 24-hour window.
  • System sleepDisable sleep mode for the duration — Rclone runs as a local process and pauses if the machine sleeps.

2. Configuration

2.1 — Install Rclone

Download the binary for your OS from the official Rclone downloads page, install or extract the executable, then open your terminal (macOS/Linux) or Command Prompt / PowerShell (Windows).

2.2 — Configure the Dropbox remote

Launch the interactive wizard with rclone config, then follow the prompts:

  1. Type n to create a new remote and name it dropbox.
  2. Choose dropbox as the storage type.
  3. Press Enter to leave client_id and client_secret blank.
  4. Type n to skip advanced config, then y for auto-config.
  5. In the browser that opens, log into Dropbox and click Allow.
  6. Back in the terminal, type y to save the remote.

2.3 — Configure the Google Drive remote

Still inside rclone config, create a second remote:

  1. Type n for a new remote and name it gdrive.
  2. Choose drive as the storage type.
  3. Press Enter to skip client_id and client_secret.
  4. For access scope, type 1 (full access to all files).
  5. Press Enter to skip the service-account file, then n to skip advanced config.
  6. Type y for auto-config; log into Google in the browser and click Allow.
  7. Type n when asked about a Shared Drive (unless migrating to an enterprise Shared Drive).
  8. Confirm, save, then type q to exit.

3. Pre-migration verification

Confirm Rclone can read both providers by listing their top-level directories:

# Check Dropbox connection
rclone lsd dropbox:
# Check Google Drive connection
rclone lsd gdrive:
Always dry-run first

Simulate the migration to confirm your paths are correct without moving any data:

rclone copy dropbox: gdrive:/DropboxBackup --dry-run -P

4. The migration command

Once the dry run succeeds, run the optimized production command:

rclone copy dropbox: gdrive:/DropboxBackup \
--fast-list \
--max-transfer 700G \
--cutoff-mode soft \
--tpslimit 4 \
--transfers 4 \
--checkers 4 \
-P

What each flag does

Flag Why it matters
--fast-listBatches directory structures, drastically cutting API calls and speeding up the initial comparison phase.
--max-transfer 700GHard ceiling that keeps you under Google’s 750 GB daily limit.
--cutoff-mode softOn hitting the limit, lets active file streams finish gracefully instead of corrupting them.
--tpslimit 4Caps transactions per second to avoid “403 User Rate Limit Exceeded” throttling.
--transfers 4Moves four files in parallel to use cloud bandwidth efficiently.
--checkers 4Runs four background integrity checks to verify file hashes match.
-PShows a live terminal UI with transfer speed, total moved, and ETA.

5. Logging & verification

Record progress to a file

Add logging flags so you can track progress or diagnose drops without keeping the terminal window open:

rclone copy dropbox: gdrive:/DropboxBackup \
--fast-list --max-transfer 700G --cutoff-mode soft \
--tpslimit 4 --transfers 4 --checkers 4 \
--log-file=migration_transfer.log \
--log-level INFO -P
  • •

Rclone Migration RunbookDropbox → OneDrive
Technical Runbook350 GB Server-to-Server Copy
Technical Runbook

Migrating Data from Dropbox to OneDrive with Rclone

A production-ready guide to moving 350 GB of data directly from Dropbox to Microsoft OneDrive. Rclone performs a server-to-server copy, so files never touch your local hard drive.

Volume
350 GB
Method
Server-to-server
Main risk
API throttling

1. Prerequisites

  • Operating systemWindows, macOS, or Linux.
  • Free storageAt least 350 GB free on the destination. A Microsoft 365 OneDrive plan typically provides 1 TB, so 350 GB fits comfortably.
  • ThrottlingOneDrive has no fixed daily upload cap, but it throttles aggressively — HTTP 429 “Too Many Requests” under load. Keep concurrency low (covered in §4).
  • File constraintsPer-file limit is 250 GB. OneDrive also rejects certain characters (< > : " | ? *) and very long paths — Rclone reports any files it must skip.
  • System sleepDisable sleep mode for the duration — Rclone runs as a local process and pauses if the machine sleeps.

2. Configuration

2.1 — Install Rclone

Download the binary for your OS from the official Rclone downloads page, install or extract the executable, then open your terminal (macOS/Linux) or Command Prompt / PowerShell (Windows).

2.2 — Configure the Dropbox remote

Launch the interactive wizard with rclone config, then follow the prompts:

  1. Type n to create a new remote and name it dropbox.
  2. Choose dropbox as the storage type.
  3. Press Enter to leave client_id and client_secret blank.
  4. Type n to skip advanced config, then y for auto-config.
  5. In the browser that opens, log into Dropbox and click Allow.
  6. Back in the terminal, type y to save the remote.

2.3 — Configure the OneDrive remote

Still inside rclone config, create a second remote:

  1. Type n for a new remote and name it onedrive.
  2. Choose onedrive as the storage type.
  3. Press Enter to skip client_id and client_secret.
  4. For the region, type 1 (Microsoft Cloud Global) unless you are on a national cloud.
  5. Type n to skip advanced config, then y for auto-config; log into Microsoft in the browser and click Accept.
  6. When asked for the account type, choose OneDrive Personal or Business (option onedrive).
  7. Rclone lists the drives it found — select the one to use (usually 0), then type y to confirm it is correct.
  8. Confirm, save, then type q to exit.

3. Pre-migration verification

Confirm Rclone can read both providers by listing their top-level directories:

# Check Dropbox connection
rclone lsd dropbox:
# Check OneDrive connection
rclone lsd onedrive:
Always dry-run first

Simulate the migration to confirm your paths are correct without moving any data:

rclone copy dropbox: onedrive:/DropboxBackup --dry-run -P

4. The migration command

Once the dry run succeeds, run the optimized production command. OneDrive’s main failure mode is throttling, so concurrency is kept deliberately low:

rclone copy dropbox: onedrive:/DropboxBackup \
--fast-list \
--tpslimit 4 \
--transfers 4 \
--checkers 4 \
--onedrive-chunk-size 250M \
-P

What each flag does

Flag Why it matters
--fast-listBatches directory structures, drastically cutting API calls and speeding up the initial comparison phase.
--tpslimit 4Caps transactions per second — the single most important flag for avoiding OneDrive’s “429 Too Many Requests” throttling.
--transfers 4Moves four files in parallel. Keep this low; raising it invites throttling rather than speed.
--checkers 4Runs four background checks comparing files between the two remotes.
--onedrive-chunk-size 250MUploads large files in 250 MB chunks, improving reliability on big transfers (must be a multiple of 320 KiB).
-PShows a live terminal UI with transfer speed, total moved, and ETA.
Hitting persistent 429 errors?

Drop to --tpslimit 2 --transfers 2. Rclone already honours OneDrive’s Retry-After headers automatically, so a throttled run slows down rather than failing.

5. Logging & verification

Record progress to a file

Add logging flags so you can track progress or diagnose drops without keeping the terminal window open:

rclone copy dropbox: onedrive:/DropboxBackup \
--fast-list --tpslimit 4 --transfers 4 --checkers 4 \
--log-file=migration_transfer.log \
--log-level INFO -P
  • •--log-file writes a plain-text record of every transaction to disk.
  • •--log-level INFO logs a confirmation line for every successfully transferred file.

Post-migration audit

After the copy finishes, run a one-way check to confirm everything on Dropbox arrived on OneDrive:

rclone check dropbox: onedrive:/DropboxBackup \
--one-way --download \
--log-file=migration_audit.log --log-level NOTICE -P
Why --download here

Dropbox and OneDrive use different hash algorithms (Dropbox’s content hash vs. OneDrive’s QuickXorHash), so Rclone cannot compare them directly. --download streams both sides and compares bytes for a true bit-for-bit audit. Omit it for a faster size-only check.

  • •--one-way verifies that everything on Dropbox reached OneDrive, ignoring extra files that may already exist there.
  • •A clean run reports 0 differences found. Any flagged omissions are listed in migration_audit.log so you can see exactly which files failed.

6. Troubleshooting & notes

Resuming interrupted transfers

Rclone operations are safe to interrupt. If the network drops or the machine shuts down, re-running the exact same command resumes the migration — already-completed files are skipped automatically.

429 / throttling errors

Expected on OneDrive under load. Rclone backs off and retries automatically; if they dominate the run, lower --tpslimit and --transfers further.

Skipped files (invalid names)

Files with characters OneDrive forbids, or paths that exceed its length limit, are reported and skipped. Review the log, rename the offenders on Dropbox, and re-run.

Out-of-memory errors

--fast-list loads the whole folder structure into RAM. With millions of tiny files this can crash Rclone — remove the flag and run again.

Data preservation

The copy command only replicates data. Your original files remain completely untouched on Dropbox.

  4. For the region, type 1 (Microsoft Cloud Global) unless you are on a national cloud.
  5. Type n to skip advanced config, then y for auto-config; log into Microsoft and click Accept.
  6. Choose OneDrive Personal or Business (option onedrive) for the account type.
  7. Select the drive Rclone lists (usually 0), then type y to confirm and save.

2.3 — Configure the Google Drive remote (destination)

Still inside rclone config, create a second remote:

  8. Confirm, save, then type q to exit.

Confirm Rclone can read both providers by listing their top-level directories:

# Check OneDrive connection
rclone lsd onedrive:
# Check Google Drive connection
rclone lsd gdrive:

rclone copy onedrive: gdrive:/OneDriveBackup --dry-run -P

4. The migration command

Once the dry run succeeds, execute the optimized production command. Because both providers throttle, concurrency is kept deliberately low:

rclone copy onedrive: gdrive:/OneDriveBackup \
--fast-list \
--max-transfer 700G \
--cutoff-mode soft \
--tpslimit 4 \
--transfers 4 \
--checkers 4 \
-P

What each flag does

Flag Why it matters
--fast-listBatches directory structures, drastically cutting API calls and speeding up the initial comparison phase.
--max-transfer 700GHard ceiling that keeps you under Google’s 750 GB daily upload limit.
--cutoff-mode softOn hitting the limit, lets active file streams finish gracefully instead of corrupting them.
--tpslimit 4Caps transactions per second — avoids both OneDrive’s “429” and Google’s “403 Rate Limit Exceeded” errors.
--transfers 4Moves four files in parallel to use bandwidth efficiently without provoking throttling.
--checkers 4Runs four background checks comparing files between the two remotes.
-PShows a live terminal UI with transfer speed, total moved, and ETA.

5. Logging & verification

Record progress to a file

Add logging flags so you can track progress or diagnose drops without keeping the terminal window open:

rclone copy onedrive: gdrive:/OneDriveBackup \
--fast-list --max-transfer 700G --cutoff-mode soft \
--tpslimit 4 --transfers 4 --checkers 4 \
--log-file=migration_transfer.log \

rclone check onedrive: gdrive:/OneDriveBackup \
--one-way --download \

Resuming interrupted transfers

Rclone operations are safe to interrupt. If the network drops or the machine shuts down, re-running the exact same command resumes the migration — already-completed files are skipped automatically.

If you migrate more than 750 GB, --max-transfer 700G stops the run cleanly. Wait 24 hours and re-run the same command — it resumes where it left off.

Expected under load from either provider. Rclone backs off and retries automatically; if they dominate the run, lower --tpslimit and --transfers further.
